item.title: Self-Hosted LACP Link Aggregation: systemd networkd vs NetworkManager vs iproute2 (2026)
item.description: Link Aggregation Control Protocol (LACP), defined in IEEE 802.3ad (now 802.1AX), combines multiple physical network interfaces into a single logical bond for increased bandwidth and redundancy. Self-hosting LACP configuration gives you control over link aggregation without relying on managed switch auto-configuration or proprietary vendor tools.

item.title: Linux Network Bonding: Active-Backup vs LACP vs Round-Robin (2026)
item.description: Network bonding (also called link aggregation or NIC teaming) combines multiple physical network interfaces into a single logical interface. This provides two key benefits: fault tolerance — if one NIC or cable fails, traffic continues on the remaining links — and increased throughput — traffic can be distributed across multiple physical links simultaneously.
